goal: At the same position, set the exposure time to 0.5 s and 2.0 s, measure once at each, compute the signal-to-noise ratio by the same method, and report the difference between the two values.

execution_summary.trajectory: Measured two spectra at the same position with different exposure times (0.5s and 2.0s), then calculated SNR using peak-to-noise ratio in run_analysis to determine the difference.
execution_summary.outcome: Measured spectra at 0.5s and 2.0s; SNR values were very similar.

lesson: Increasing exposure from 0.5s to 2s at this specific position did not significantly improve the SNR (difference ~0.16), suggesting that the noise might be dominated by something other than photon shot noise or that the signal is already well-captured.
